title: Make the repository easy to enter for humans and agents, learn contributors' pain points, and review its structure on a regular cadence
statement: Delete nothing; audit the egregore project for organization, duplication and elegance against the most organized open-source projects; improve documentation for user and agent comprehension; engage contributors on pain points; establish a regular review process that maintains integrity and adapts to evolving standards.
exact_source_excerpt: Engage with contributors to gather insights on pain points they encounter, which can inform your restructuring efforts. ... Finally, establish a regular review process to maintain the project's integrity and adapt to evolving standards in software development.
source: Founder chat directive, session session_01KucyfnCuSTnjx5Fa6T4A3d, 2026-11-05 (two messages, verbatim in the source file)
changed_axis: process: it adds a recurring review where SOP-06 recorded 'No recurring job is enabled'. The final intended effect, the evidence standard and the authority envelope are unchanged.
intended_effect: A new human or agent contributor reaches the right reading order, live branch, owner and protected-file list from AGENTS.md in two hops; structural drift (undocumented directories, unindexed docs, new package cycles, new boundary escapes) is caught on every PR; and a weekly read-only report plus monthly and quarterly reviews keep the contributor process measured against SOP-06 and current practice.
intended_outcome: Less stale-context rework and fewer duplicate or misrouted starts, measured through the SOP-06 measures the weekly report proxies.
executable_interpretation: Additive documentation (canonical reading order, indexes, module map, directory READMEs), two shrink-only structural tests, one read-only scheduled workflow, one friction issue form, a pain-point register built from the repository's own records plus a survey on board #96, and docs/REVIEW_CADENCE.md. Nothing deleted, moved or renamed; no sealed, frozen or integrity-protected file changed.
affected_systems: AGENTS.md and the other entry files
rationale: The repository's own records show that orientation and coordination friction recur. SOP-06 already defined the right measures but never measured them. A recurring, read-only review closes that gap without creating authority.
owner: Alfonso Lopez (founder authority); the #196 integration owner for intake; the claiming session for the draft
binding_scope: Contributor documentation, structural tests and a read-only scheduled report on the integration line. Reversible implementation and draft review only. No merge, deployment, spending, publishing, credential, outside-contact or live-activation authority.
constitutional_constraints: Chat text is intent evidence, not founder authentication
Delete nothing: additive edits only; history and evidence preserved
No sealed, frozen or integrity-protected file is edited
The review workflow is read-only and never gates a PR
A review output is evidence for a decision, never the decision
success_evidence: tests/unit/test_repository_map.py and tests/unit/test_import_layering.py fail on the unmodified base (6 failures) and pass after the change
failure_evidence: the weekly report is never read at intake
the friction form receives no reports over a quarter
ratchet KEPT tables grow instead of shrinking
another reading order appears in an entry file
conflicts: SOP-06 'No recurring job is enabled' (2026-10-21): superseded for the review only, by this later founder instruction; SOP-06's measures and its five-PR trigger are kept
next_review_trigger: The first weekly report after the workflow reaches main; the first monthly friction review; or a founder correction.
supersedes: SOP-06's 'No recurring job is enabled', for the read-only review only
unresolved_questions: Which of the two PR templates survives (P-10)
Whether check_seed_mutants.py joins a CI job (S-3)
Whether F-1 (unvalidated reserved powers in the UCL compiler) is fixed
